name: Morgan Day
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember buying corsages for girls who came without escorts.” People around Studio Boulevard know Morgan by a small Thursday habit. Morgan waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I wrote the school's old dance rule years ago. I wanted daughters without dates to feel welcome.
appearance: Morgan has a small notch in the left eyebrow. Look for salt-and-pepper curls. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a striped cotton shirt with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. In conversation Morgan draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting.
personality: Morgan is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Morgan asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To explain what the rule originally tried to protect.
family: Seth Roberts is Morgan’s first cousin once removed. Morgan can always ask for five minutes alone. Seth asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Midnight cinnamon*, Seth says, “I hated that holiday until the sack opened.”
connections: Noel Mota. The ceremony organizer asks the retired author of the rule what it was designed to protect.

reactions.situation: One of the fathers misses the dance rehearsal
reactions.response: Morgan keeps the missed step available for a quiet practice before the ceremony.

reactions.situation: A neighbor offers to pay for a favor that was meant kindly
reactions.response: Morgan asks for help with a task the neighbor does well, so both people get to contribute something.
